s.description: Evaluate and enforce sync patterns optimized for Cloudflare: Durable Objects (WebSocket coordination), Queues (async messaging), D1 (edge DB), Workers (edge compute), KV (config propagation). Covers real-time sync, eventual consistency, conflict handling, contract validation, and cross-layer coordination.

scope.directories: sync/, services/, api/, lib/, workers/, durable-objects/

cloudflare_context.assumption: This project uses Cloudflare as primary infrastructure provider

product.name: Durable Objects
product.notes: Single-threaded per ID. Natural WebSocket coordinator for real-time sync. Transactional SQL storage for sync state. Use for: room-based sync, collaborative editing, presence.

product.name: Queues
product.notes: At-least-once delivery. Batch processing. Retry with backoff. Dead letter queues. Use for: system-to-system sync, webhook processing, eventual consistency.

product.name: D1
product.notes: SQLite at the edge. Read replicas for geographic distribution. Use as sync target for persistent state.

product.name: Workers
product.notes: Sync API endpoints. WebSocket upgrade handling. SSE streaming. Webhook receivers.

product.name: KV
product.notes: Eventually consistent (up to 60s). Global propagation. Use for: feature flags, config sync, non-critical state. NOT for transactional sync.

product.name: Pub/Sub
product.notes: MQTT-compatible. Use for: broadcast sync, IoT, real-time notifications.

product.name: Hyperdrive
product.role: Database connection pooling to external DBs
product.notes: Connection pooling + caching for external Postgres/MySQL. Use when syncing with external DB that isn't D1.

pattern.name: do-websocket-hub
pattern.description: Durable Object as real-time sync coordinator via WebSocket
pattern.flow: Client -> Worker (upgrade) -> Durable Object (WebSocket) -> broadcast to connected clients

pattern.name: queue-event-sync
pattern.use_when: Webhook processing, third-party integration, eventual consistency acceptable
pattern.flow: Producer Worker -> Queue -> Consumer Worker -> D1/R2

pattern.name: d1-read-replica
pattern.description: D1 read replicas for geographic data distribution
pattern.flow: Write to primary D1 -> automatic replication to read replicas

pattern.name: kv-config-propagation
pattern.description: KV for eventually consistent config/flag sync
pattern.use_when: Feature flags, runtime config, non-critical metadata
pattern.flow: Admin writes to KV -> propagates globally (up to 60s)

sync_system.requirement: MANDATORY: Sync must be intentional, observable, schema-aware, and use the right Cloudflare primitive for each sync pattern.

spec_document.format:
## Sync Topology (Cloudflare) | Entity | Direction | Transport | CF Product | Consistency | Contract | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Collaborative doc | Bidirectional | WebSocket | Durable Objects | Causal (CRDT) | Yjs update binary | | User profile | Unidirectional | REST | D1 + Workers | Strong (single primary) | Zod schema v2 | | Webhooks inbound | Unidirectional | Queue | Queues + Workers | Eventual | JSON Schema v1 | | Feature flags | Unidirectional | KV propagation | KV | Eventual (60s) | TypeScript enum |
## Schema Contract per Sync Boundary ## Idempotency Strategy ## Failure Modes & Retry (Queues DLQ) ## Observability (Analytics Engine) ## Connected Systems (backup-specs.md, state-specs.md)

architecture_principles.principle: DO for real-time coordination. Queues for async. KV for config. D1 for persistence. Don't use KV for transactional sync. Don't use DO for batch processing.
Sync replicates current state. Backup preserves point-in-time. They solve different problems.
Every sync boundary validates schema. DO WebSocket messages validated. Queue messages validated. Webhook payloads validated.
Queues deliver at-least-once. WebSocket reconnects may replay. Every sync op must be safe to retry.
If you can't measure sync lag, you can't know it works. Analytics Engine metrics mandatory.
Queue DLQ configured. WebSocket errors surfaced. Sync failures observable.

anti_patterns.violation: Using KV for transactional sync (60s eventual consistency = data loss in concurrent scenarios)
Durable Object WebSocket sync with no conflict resolution (concurrent edits = silent overwrites)
Queue consumer with no payload validation (shape mismatch = silent corruption)
No idempotency handling on Queue consumer (at-least-once = duplicates)
Durable Object WebSocket with no reconnection protocol (client reconnects lose state)
No sync lag metric via Analytics Engine
No Queue DLQ configured (poison messages block consumer)
WebSocket messages not schema-validated (version drift between clients)
No backpressure on DO WebSocket broadcast (slow clients block fast ones)
Sync docs out of date with implementation
No drift detection between synced systems

criterion.name: Sync Primitive Selection
criterion.grade: Wrong CF product for the job (KV for transactional sync, DO for batch, etc.)
Partially correct but some mismatches; not leveraging CF-native features
Correct primitives for most flows; some sub-optimal choices
Right primitive per sync pattern; documented rationale
Optimal selection with clear rationale; leverages CF-native features (DO WebSocket, Queue retry, KV propagation)
Architecture demonstrates deep CF platform knowledge; primitives composed for capabilities beyond individual product limits; patterns reusable across projects

criterion.name: Sync Contract Clarity
criterion.grade: No explicit contract; WebSocket messages untyped; Queue payloads unvalidated
Some typing but no runtime validation at sync boundary
Contracts exist but not enforced at DO/Queue boundary
Versioned contracts with runtime validation on all sync paths
Contract-first; producer and consumer validate; breaking changes caught in CI
Contracts auto-generated; sync adapters derived from schema; zero shape mismatch possible

criterion.name: Idempotency & Ordering
criterion.grade: Queue replay produces duplicates; DO reconnects replay without dedup
Some idempotency but inconsistent; no keys on WebSocket messages
Idempotency keys present; dedup on most paths
All sync mutations idempotent; dedup tracked in D1; Queue at-least-once handled
Provably idempotent; causal ordering in DO; exactly-once via dedup + idempotency
Deterministic replay; any message sequence produces identical state; formal verification

criterion.name: Failure Handling (Queues, DO, WebSocket)
criterion.grade: No DLQ on Queue; DO WebSocket errors swallowed; no retry
Basic retry; no DLQ; poison messages crash consumer
Queue DLQ configured; WebSocket reconnect works; some gaps
Robust retry + DLQ + alerting; WebSocket reconnect with state recovery; circuit breaker
Self-healing; DLQ reprocessing; split-brain detection in DO; chaos-tested
Adaptive failure handling; auto-rerouting; zero manual intervention; continuous chaos engineering

criterion.name: Sync Observability
criterion.grade: No metrics; sync health unknown
console.log; no structured metrics
Some Analytics Engine metrics; no lag measurement
Sync lag via Analytics Engine; health checks; alerting on failure
Real-time lag; drift detection; SLO on freshness; automated remediation
Predictive; anomaly detection on lag; sync health as SLI with error budget

criterion.name: Cache Invalidation Coordination
criterion.grade: Sync updates D1 but KV/client cache stale
Some invalidation; inconsistent across sync paths
Most paths invalidate; edge cases stale
Comprehensive invalidation; sync events purge KV + client cache
Sync-driven invalidation across all layers (D1 -> KV -> client)
Invalidation derived from sync events; zero config per-entity; sub-second freshness

criterion.name: Sync-Backup Boundary
criterion.grade: Sync conflated with backup; "we have D1 replicas" = "we have backups"
Awareness but not documented
Separate backup exists; boundary informal
sync-specs.md and backup-specs.md cross-reference; clear boundary
Explicit boundary with rationale; each tested independently
Unified data lifecycle; sync = freshness, backup = durability; formally defined

criterion.name: Connected System Awareness
criterion.grade: Sync isolated; no cross-references
Informal awareness
sync-specs.md exists, no cross-refs
Cross-references backup-specs.md, state-specs.md; CF product roles mapped
Integrated spec graph; sync decisions informed by state/backup topology
Unified data architecture; all specs are facets of single coherent system

standardization_check.step: Inventory all sync paths: identify DO WebSocket, Queue, KV propagation, external webhook
Verify correct CF primitive per sync pattern (no KV for transactional, no DO for batch)
Verify schema validation at every sync boundary (DO message, Queue payload, webhook body)
Verify idempotency on all sync mutations (especially Queue at-least-once)
Verify DO WebSocket reconnection protocol exists
Verify sync lag metrics via Analytics Engine
Verify sync events trigger cache invalidation (KV, client)
Verify sync is NOT conflated with backup
